label: conj:geom-universality
title: Universality of $\mathrm{Geom}(K)$: the categorical volume form yields $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ and $\mathrm{CS}(K)$
html:
Conjecture (universality of \mathrm{Geom}(K), conditional on hyperbolic volume transcendence). The categorical volume form, evaluated on the knot complement S^3 \setminus K through the fibre functor \tau, yields \mathrm{Vol}(K) for hyperbolic knots and \mathrm{CS}(K) for torus knots. This identification is universal: it provides the unique evaluation compatible with the Frobenius--Hopf structure.

Specifically, \mathrm{Geom}(K) is the unique functional on knot complements satisfying:

  1. Additivity: \mathrm{Geom}(K_1 \# K_2) = \mathrm{Geom}(K_1) + \mathrm{Geom}(K_2).
  2. Functoriality: \mathrm{Geom}(K) = \tau(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\mathcal{B}_K))) for some fibre functor \tau.
  3. Normalization: \mathrm{Geom}(\bigcirc) = 0 (vacuum) and \mathrm{Geom}(4_1) = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 (fixes q_0).

Proof sketch. We divide the supporting argument into three steps; it is a sketch, not a complete proof.

Step 1: Existence (Neumann--Zagier, τ-image side). On the τ-image side, the Neumann--Zagier theorem establishes that for a hyperbolic knot K, \mathrm{Vol}(K) and \mathrm{CS}(K) are related by the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm. This is a function of the \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) representation variety. In the categorical framework, the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A at parameter q has a representation variety isomorphic to \mathrm{Spec} of the coordinate ring \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2). The fibre functor \tau evaluates the volume form \omega on this variety. By Neumann--Zagier, the real part of this evaluation is \mathrm{Vol}(K).

Step 2: Uniqueness (Yekutieli rigidity). The rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet provides a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing \langle -, - \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}. Yekutieli's rigidity theorem shows that this pairing is unique up to a scalar. The scalar is fixed by the normalizations \mathrm{Geom}(\bigcirc) = 0 and \mathrm{Geom}(4_1) = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2. Therefore any functional satisfying properties 1--3 must equal \mathrm{Geom}.

Step 3: The CS/Vol duality. For torus knots, \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and the representation variety consists of a single abelian flat connection. The evaluation of \omega_A^\bullet on this connection yields the Chern--Simons functional. The duality \mathrm{Vol}/\hbar_q^2 \leftrightarrow \mathrm{CS} \cdot \hbar_q^2 follows from the self-duality of the rigid dualizing complex. Additivity follows from the fact that connected sum corresponds to tensor product in the Frobenius--Hopf category, and the volume form is a trace.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
heading: Conjecture
